description: I am an independent builder fascinated by using AI and data to help people make faster, safer decisions from satellite observations. I like turning messy scientific data into tools that are clear, honest about their limits, and truly useful. I want to build a web app that gives emergency managers a trustworthy view of fire activity over time. I am looking for teammates in remote sensing, statistics, map frontend, or design who want to build something rigorous.
summary: Satellites have tracked fires since 2002, but the older MODIS sensor and the newer VIIRS sensor count fires differently, so joining their records makes it look as if fires jumped when VIIRS arrived. Quorivis fixes this. It counts burning grid cells per day instead of raw pixels, calibrates VIIRS to MODIS units for any area and calendar month, and shows one consistent series from 2002 to October 2026. Users pick a region of India or draw their own area and get a burning calendar, a "versus usual" view that shows unusual months, a day and night split, and a test on years the method never saw. For India, the typical error on a held-out month is about 10% and on a yearly total about 4%. It matters because emergency managers and researchers need a fire history they can trust across the sensor change.
details:
What it does: Quorivis merges NASA MODIS and VIIRS active fire detections for India into one monthly record from 2002 to October 2026. Users choose a region or draw an area on the map and see a chart with a 90% range, a year-by-month burning calendar (counts, or how each month compares with the usual for that month), a table of the last 12 months, a day and night split, and downloadable CSV files.

How it works: Each detection is placed on a 0.01 degree grid, and a cell with a detection on a day counts once, which removes the resolution advantage of VIIRS. For the chosen area, time of day and calendar month, VIIRS is scaled to MODIS units using calibration years 2013 to 2020. The scaled VIIRS series continues the Aqua MODIS record. After Suomi NPP stopped delivering data on 2 November 2026, the series continues with NOAA-20. The newest months use near-real-time data and are marked provisional.

Validation: Each calibration year is held out in turn and predicted from the others. For India the typical error is about 10% for a single month and 4% for a yearly total, with a rank correlation of 0.99. Night is harder (about 30% for a month), and the app warns when a view is less reliable. In Punjab and Haryana, Aqua compared with calibrated VIIRS rises from 1.08 in 2021 to 1.54 in 2025, which points to the older MODIS sensor changing over time.

Benefits: A fire history that is comparable across sensors, with its uncertainty shown, for emergency managers, land managers and researchers.

What we hope to achieve: Extend the same method to more countries and keep the record updated as new data arrives.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the app; Python (pandas, numpy) to prepare the data; GitHub Pages for hosting; Canva for the demo slides; Fraunces and IBM Plex Sans fonts. result analysis and documentation were developed with AI (Claude) assistance.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS: MODIS Collection 6.1 active fire detections (Aqua), 2002 to 2026. and VIIRS 375 m active fire detections (Suomi NPP and NOAA-20), 2012 to 2026
projectRefs: Schroeder, W., Oliva, P., Giglio, L., & Csiszar, I. A. (2014). The new VIIRS 375 m active fire detection data product.
Giglio, L., Schroeder, W., & Justice, C. O. (2016). The collection 6 MODIS active fire detection algorithm and fire products.
